ordered legacy claim handoff and replay

Implement ordered legacy claim handoff and replay. Rework normal presence/READY replay and result acknowledgement using existing owned-claim/managed-tab lease checks. Keep claim and renewal alive on transport failure or foreign lease, and separate accepted task rejection from transient delivery. Acknowledge the previous RESULT before dispatching a successor. Treat an occupied content task as retryable without consuming an attempt. Recheck synchronous Stop intent immediately before dispatch, including when a caller supplies a readiness probe. Verify through the normal entry points. #114: Reject an owned claim replay message, then restore readiness; assert ownership/renewal survive and no task failure is posted. Demonstrate actual accepted task rejection retains its old outcome. #115: Queue two tasks and assert the first acknowledgement reaches content before the next assignment is accepted; a busy content key consumes no attempt. #116: Restore a held claim alongside a different lease owner; check zero dispatch/fail, then release or replace with matching task and tab and check one replay. #138: Raise Stop while READY is waiting on storage/reconciliation with a supplied probe; assert zero replay and successful cleanup. Compare ordinary READY. Work in the extension source and its local tests. Use generated DOM fixtures, mocked browser/storage/transport APIs and fake clocks as appropriate. Keep verification offline and use fictional records. Do not contact any live service, use credentials or customer data, or operate a real account. Inspect current implementation before editing. Report the changed files, commands actually run, per-issue assertions and any unverified acceptance criteria.

Target issues: #114, #115, #116, #138. Lead this issue group as gpt-6.2-astra at ultra effort. Use gpt-6.2-sol developers at max effort with separate file ownership and independent verification. Use the repository's normal local checks and generated synthetic fixtures. First inspect the current code and tests; when the base already satisfies an item, establish that directly. Retain existing fixes. For each numbered issue report its concrete behavior, tracked regression coverage and the exact commands and outcomes. Run the repository's complete affected test suites and update generated content hashes where required. Do not deploy, use production systems, change external settings or publish sensitive data. Finish on your result branch.
